analysis.title: Nonfarm Validates December Hike — Cue Inflation
key_insights: October nonfarm payrolls rose 165k versus Scotia's 100k estimate and consensus of 70k. The unemployment rate fell to 4.1% versus 4.2% expected.
The prior month was revised to 60k from 29k. The two-month payroll revision totals +84k, which adds to the case for a Fed hike in December pending next week's CPI.
19bps of a hike is priced for December, and short-term bond yields are rising on the report.

Business services and education and health services drove most of the gain. Health and social services added 55k, the fastest hiring pace since April, including 42k health care jobs (16k at hospitals, 11k in home health, 5k in outpatient centres).

Professional and business services rose 70k, more than anticipated, and explain most of the overshoot versus Scotia's estimate. Gains came from professional, scientific and technical services (33k), admin support and waste management (28k) and company management (9k).
Average hourly wages rose 4.5% m/m SAAR in October after 3.2% in September, so wage growth is accelerating.
Hours worked rose 0.1% m/m in October and track a 1.2% q/q SAAR gain in Q4, close to the prior 1.3%, which supports solid GDP growth.
The unemployment rate fell to 4.1% because the household survey showed a 463k job gain, which exceeded the 421k labour force expansion.

Scotia expects more elevated health sector hiring because the respiratory virus season started earlier than normal. Unadjusted October health hiring was elevated, but a relatively low seasonal adjustment factor dampened the effect.
No clear weather effect appeared despite a mild fall. Leisure and hospitality fell 13k, retail rose 6k and construction fell 3k. Scotia asks whether the effect comes later with El Niño.
Under-sampling on first pass will continue to drive high revision risk in future payroll reports.
The FOMC is focused on inflation, but a solid job market adds to the hawkish case.
